title_en: Japan's 2026 trade-insurance rules: special underwriting for supply-chain security

quick_take.what_changed: Japan's 2026 trade-insurance reform introduces a special underwriting framework linked to specified government-to-government arrangements. The June consultation proposed implementing rules for approvals, accounting and risk governance; the final ordinance requires further text-level checking.
quick_take.who_is_affected: Japan's export-credit insurer NEXI is directly affected; companies seeking cover for qualifying international projects may be indirectly affected, depending on the final criteria.
quick_take.what_to_do_now: Distinguish the enacted statutory framework from the consultation draft, and verify the operative ordinance, ministerial notices and individual underwriting criteria before assuming a project qualifies.

instruments.name_en: 2026 METI Ordinance No. 64 amending the Enforcement Regulation of the Trade Insurance Act

paragraphs: Japan's trade insurance system provides public export-credit insurance through Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI). The government's June 2026 explanation links a new category of special underwriting to the need to strengthen Japanese companies' supply chains and develop overseas demand for Japanese machinery and other products. It is not a general-purpose subsidy for all foreign investment.

The June consultation proposed a ring-fenced special account for special underwriting, separate from NEXI's other operations. The stated architecture also included government bonds that could be issued and delivered to the company until 31 March 2029. These mechanisms address the tension between pursuing strategic transactions and isolating the resulting financial risks. The proposal alone does not prove the exact final operative wording.

The consultation proposed an approval application for individual special underwriting decisions, registration of delivered government bonds, accounting allocation rules, and ministerial guidance on credit, liquidity and foreign-exchange risk. Its proposed designated arrangement was the Japan–US memorandum of understanding on strategic investment signed on 4 September 2025. Whether every proposed detail was adopted must be checked against the final promulgated instruments.

The underlying amendment to the Trade Insurance Act formed part of the industrial-competitiveness reform legislation passed on 29 May 2026, according to METI's official consultation overview. That overview explicitly connected the new underwriting category with government-to-government arrangements judged particularly necessary for Japanese supply-chain resilience.

On 22 June 2026, METI opened consultation on five connected instruments: amendments to the Trade Insurance Act enforcement regulation, amendments to NEXI's accounting regulation, a ministerial notice designating an arrangement, a special-underwriting business guideline, and special-underwriting standards. The consultation closed on 21 July 2026.

The e-Gov consultation results published on 31 July 2026 identify five promulgated instruments: METI Ordinances Nos. 64 and 65, and METI Notices Nos. 96, 97 and 98. Two submissions were received. METI reported no changes in response to comments, while noting technical revisions without substantive effect. The e-Gov law-update record identifies Ordinance No. 64 as effective on 31 July 2026. These records establish promulgation and consultation outcome, but do not by themselves establish the detailed wording of each final provision.

confirmed.text: The official consultation closed on 21 July 2026.
The e-Gov law-update record identifies 31 July 2026 as the promulgation and effective date of METI Ordinance No. 64; the precise amended provisions still require direct inspection.
On 31 July 2026 METI published consultation results identifying two submitted opinions, no changes in response to opinions, and non-substantive technical revisions to the five instruments.

expected: Before publication, compare the final ordinance and related ministerial notices against the June draft, and identify any transitional provisions.
uncertainties: The results notice identifies the five promulgated instruments and the absence of substantive consultation-driven changes, but the complete final operative text of each instrument and any transitional provisions still require article-by-article inspection before publication.
Whether the 2025 Japan–US memorandum is designated in the final notice and whether any exceptions or transitional rules apply remains to be confirmed.

paragraphs: NEXI's special underwriting would operate through a distinct decision and financial-risk framework rather than automatically extending ordinary trade insurance to every transaction. For exporters and sponsors, eligibility depends on the actual government arrangement and the applicable final underwriting standards.

The proposed ring-fenced accounting, approval and risk-reporting provisions would change the internal governance of the public insurer, not directly impose a universal filing duty on all exporters. The final legal effect must be determined from the promulgated instruments.
checklist: For a proposed insured transaction, identify the government-to-government arrangement and document the connection to Japanese supply-chain resilience or overseas demand.
Request the operative NEXI underwriting terms rather than relying on the June 2026 draft or assuming approval is automatic.
Check final ministerial notices, applicable approval procedure and financial-risk conditions before treating special underwriting as available.
